front: Scientific names: African elephant and white rhino

back: Communal Areas Management Programme for Indigenous Resources: communities manage and benefit from wildlife (tourism, hunting income).
Environmental impact assessments, pollution and waste regulation, monitoring, enforcement of environmental law, education.
Appendix I: commercial international trade banned. Appendix II: trade only with permits showing it is not harmful.
Removes the poachers' reward; horn is keratin and regrows, so it is repeated.
Poaching (ivory, horn), habitat loss, human-wildlife conflict, drought; slow breeding slows recovery.
Above carrying capacity, elephants destroy woodland, harming other species, and raid crops more often.
For sales: fund conservation from stockpiles. Against: may raise demand and help launder illegal ivory.
Elephant: gestation about 22 months, calf every 4-5 years. White rhino: about 16 months, calf every 2-3 years.
